Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

fastsae 1.0.0

Estimation engines for hb_area(), hb_unit() and hb_twofold()

  • New argument engine, taking an engine object from the new constructors inla_engine() and jax_engine() (or the strings "inla", the default, and "jax" for their default settings). Each constructor holds all settings of its engine, so hb_area() itself only describes the model:
    • inla_engine(strategy, link, scale_model, prior_prec, prior_phi, prior_rho, prior_prec_time, prior_rho_time, prior_prec_subarea, draws, seed, ...), where ... goes to INLA::inla(). control.* lists given there are merged with the package defaults (before, they clashed with them in hb_area() and replaced them in hb_unit()/hb_twofold()). Priors and draws left at NULL take the default of the model function, so the defaults of each function are unchanged; settings a function does not use are ignored with a warning.
    • jax_engine(warmup, samples, chains, device, seed, prior_beta, robust, keep_draws, progress) fits the same area-level models by full MCMC (NumPyro NUTS on JAX: CPU, NVIDIA GPU or the Apple silicon GPU via device = "metal") through ‘reticulate’ (Suggests); the engine formerly shipped in the separate ‘fastsaegpu’ package now lives in fastsae. It supports all six families, bym2/bym/besag/generic1 (alias "leroux"), rw1/ar1/iid and every st_interaction, plus prior_beta = "horseshoe" and robust = TRUE (Student-t area effects). Results have the same structure as the INLA engine, with the posterior draws in draws, the largest split R-hat in rhat_max (convergence is rhat_max < 1.05), and DIC/WAIC in goodness. Posterior self-benchmarking (also by benchmark_group) adjusts the MCMC draws exactly as for INLA, and benchmark_sae() uses the draws for the MSE matrix.
    • The engine settings are returned in engine_spec; engine holds the engine name.
  • hb_unit() and hb_twofold() take the same engine = inla_engine(...) (INLA only). In hb_twofold(), prior_prec_area is now inla_engine(prior_prec = ), n_samples is inla_engine(draws = ), and the posterior draws for the area aggregates honour seed. Their results carry engine and engine_spec too.
  • jax_engine(device = "metal") now samples on the Apple GPU. jax-metal cannot compile two operations of NumPyro’s NUTS sampler (the popcnt bit count, and lax.cond statements whose outputs are constants), so fits used to fall back to the CPU. fastsae now replaces both with equivalent operations that Metal can compile, and steps the chains from Python; the draws match the CPU sampler. On an Apple M4, Metal is faster than the CPU for large models (about 2x at 10,000 domains) and slower for small ones, where a fixed cost of about two minutes per fit dominates (see the “hb_area() engines” benchmark article). device = "auto" keeps using the CPU on macOS.
  • New setup_numpyro_env() and check_numpyro_available() to install and check the Python side. Nothing is installed or downloaded unless setup_numpyro_env() is called.
  • The frequentist lme4 GLMM route (method = "laplace" for non-spatial binomial and Poisson models) has been removed; such models are now fitted by INLA. ‘lme4’ moved to Suggests.
  • Deprecated: method (method = "laplace" becomes engine = inla_engine(strategy = "laplace")), and passing strategy, link, scale_model, prior_*, benchmark_draws, benchmark_seed, n_samples or INLA::inla() arguments directly to hb_area(), hb_unit() or hb_twofold(). They still work, with a warning, and are forwarded to inla_engine().
  • print()/summary() show the engine, and the self-benchmarking line now names the method used (posterior draws or Wang-Fuller-Qu) instead of always reporting Wang-Fuller-Qu.

Statistical corrections (mathematical audit)

  • eblup_stfh(): the analytical g3g_3 was computed with the wrong matrix orientation ((KaΨVΨKb)ii(K_a \Psi V \Psi K_b)_{ii} instead of ψi2(KaVKb)ii\psi_i^2 (K_a V K_b)_{ii}), which is wrong whenever vardir is heterogeneous. g3g_3 now uses the exact derivative of the EBLUP, ∂θ̃/∂θa=ΨPVaPy\partial\tilde\theta/\partial\theta_a = \Psi P V_a P y, and the REML information at the final estimates.

  • eblup_stfh() bootstrap MSE: the variance components are now re-estimated in every replicate (before, they were held fixed, so the bootstrap missed the g3g_3 contribution), and the SAR effects are generated with the lower Cholesky factor (before, Var(u1)=RR′≠Ω1\mathrm{Var}(u_1) = RR' \ne \Omega_1).

  • eblup_stfh() now sorts the panel internally into the domain-major order the model requires and returns results in the caller’s row order. Before, unsorted input was silently mis-specified – including the time-major mys_panel used in the examples, tests and vignette (where sae::eblupSTFH(), which assumes domain-major data, gave the same wrong fit).

  • eblup_stfh(): when the classical Fisher scoring fails, or converges to a negative variance that would only be truncated to 0, the fit switches to constrained REML (variances >= 0, |rho| <= 0.999; projected scoring with step halving), which returns the actual constrained maximiser. Convergence in a simulation went from 63% to 99% of the replicates; fits on which the classical iteration converges to an interior point are unchanged (identical to sae::eblupSTFH()). A correlation whose variance is 0 is unidentified and gets an NA standard error.

  • eblup_stfh() bootstrap: non-converged replicates are replaced by new draws until B valid replicates are obtained (as in the SFH bootstrap).

  • eblup_twofold(): the analytical MSE estimator is now g1+g2+2g3g_1 + g_2 + 2 g_3 (REML) and g1+g2+2g3−bML′∇g1g_1 + g_2 + 2 g_3 - b_{ML}'\nabla g_1 (ML); before it was g1+g2+g3g_1 + g_2 + g_3, which ignores the downward bias of the plug-in g1g_1. The REML Fisher information now includes the cross-area terms.

  • eblup_sfh() with unsampled domains: the SAR process is defined on all domains of W, so the sampled domains are now fitted with the marginal covariance σ2Σfull[s,s]\sigma^2 \Sigma_{full}[s,s] (before: the SAR built from the sub-matrix W[s,s]), consistent with the kriging of the unsampled domains and the bootstrap.

  • eblup_sfh(): an upper-boundary ρ̂=0.999\hat\rho = 0.999 is no longer mapped to 11 (singular for a row-standardised W); bootstrap replicates are no longer rejected when estimates exceed 1e6 (scale-dependent check); npbmse no longer fails when σ̂u2=0\hat\sigma^2_u = 0.

  • hb_unit() with popsize_var: the non-sampled part is now predicted at the non-sampled covariate mean x‾d,r=(NdX‾d−ndx‾d,s)/(Nd−nd)\bar x_{d,r} = (N_d \bar X_d - n_d \bar x_{d,s})/(N_d - n_d) (before: at X‾d\bar X_d), and its posterior SD includes σe2/(Nd−nd)\sigma_e^2/(N_d - n_d).

  • hb_unit() (Gaussian, non-spatial): INLA’s posterior mode search now starts at the REML estimates of the nested error model. Under the vague log-gamma prior it could stall near σu2=0\sigma^2_u = 0 depending on the number of threads (e.g. σ̂u2≈1\hat\sigma^2_u \approx 1 instead of ≈68\approx 68 on cornsoybean). A control.mode passed through inla_engine() takes precedence.

  • benchmark_sae(method = "optimal"): the adjustment is now proportional to wiMSEiw_i\,\mathrm{MSE}_i, the minimiser of ∑i(θi′−θ̂i)2/MSEi\sum_i (\theta_i' - \hat\theta_i)^2/\mathrm{MSE}_i subject to the benchmark (before: MSEi/wi\mathrm{MSE}_i / w_i). Results are unchanged for equal weights.

  • eblup_twofold() with one subarea per area (only s2v + s2u identified): Fisher scoring uses the pseudo-inverse of the singular information.

  • eblup_bhf(): the bootstrap MSE now uses the same population means (popnmean_xpop) as the estimate.

  • eblup_fh(transform = "log"): documentation now describes the back-transformation accurately (conditional-mean correction exp⁡(μ̃+g1/2)\exp(\tilde\mu + g_1/2) with delta-method MSE; not the full Slud-Maiti second-order correction), and self-benchmarking warns that the constraint holds on the log scale only.

  • eblup_fh(transform = "log"): unsampled domains now always use the synthetic correction exp⁡(x′β̂+σ̂u2/2)\exp(x'\hat\beta + \hat\sigma^2_u/2), even when their vardir is supplied.

  • HB models: reported variance components are posterior means of the variance, E[1/τ∣y]E[1/\tau \mid y], instead of 1/E[τ∣y]1/E[\tau \mid y].

  • eblup_stfh() analytical MSE now includes the second-derivative term g4g_4 (V is nonlinear in ρ1,ρ2\rho_1, \rho_2), as the SFH MSE does: mse = g1 + g2 + 2 g3 - g4, with g4 returned. Simulation: relative bias -1.7% (was +2.4% without g4g_4, -6.1% without g3g_3).

  • eblup_sfh(): when the classical Fisher scoring fails or ends with σ̂2<0\hat\sigma^2 < 0, the (RE)ML likelihood is maximised under the constraints (as for eblup_stfh()), also inside the bootstrap. An estimate at ρ=−0.999\rho = -0.999 is reported as −1-1 only when I+WI + W is non-singular (not for bipartite graphs such as a rook grid, where it made the bootstrap MSE explode).

  • eblup_sfh() unsampled (kriged) domains: the analytical MSE now includes g3g_3 (exact derivative of the kriging predictor) and the second-order bias of the plug-in g1g_1 (and the ML bias term): g1 + g2 + g3 - tr(I^{-1} Hess g1)/2. Simulation (REML): relative bias -3.8% (was -7.5%).

  • eblup_sfh() / eblup_stfh() analytical MSE: a correlation estimated on the boundary (|ρ̂|≥0.999|\hat\rho| \ge 0.999, or reported as −1-1) is treated as fixed – only the information block of the other parameters is inverted – because the Prasad-Rao expansion is not valid there and could explode. The SE of such a ρ\rho is NA. For SFH this departs from sae::mseSFH in that case only (interior estimates still agree exactly).

  • eblup_sfh(method = "ML") analytical MSE: g3g_3 and the ML bias term bML=12I−1hb_{ML} = \frac12 I^{-1} h now use the ML information instead of the REML one (as sae::mseSFH does). With σ̂2≈0\hat\sigma^2 \approx 0 and ρ̂≈1\hat\rho \approx 1 the REML choice made the bias term explode (MSE up to 10610^6 in simulations); with few domains the ML information also reduced the median MSE bias (e.g. +3.6% vs +6.5%, m=36m = 36). The ML MSE therefore no longer equals sae::mseSFH; REML is unchanged.

  • eblup_stfh() is much faster: REML scores and Fisher information are computed from the block structure of VV (domain blocks plus a rank-DD spatial part) without forming M×MM \times M matrices (O(TD3+M(D+p)2)O(T D^3 + M(D+p)^2) instead of O(M3)O(M^3) per iteration; identical results). Fitting the 40×1140 \times 11mys_panel went from about 7.7 s to 0.4 s, and the parametric bootstrap (which re-estimates the model in every replicate) from about 2.4 s to 0.4 s per replicate.

  • hb_area(self_benchmark = TRUE) now benchmarks every posterior draw by default (benchmark_method = "posterior"; difference / logit / ratio adjustment by family), so the constraint is exact for every likelihood and SD / credible intervals refer to the benchmarked estimator. Benchmark targets are computed on the parameter scale (proportions for binomial, rates for counts with exposure); before, the WFQ targets used counts while the estimates were proportions / rates. benchmark_method = "wfq" keeps the previous augmented-model approach.

  • eblup_fh(transform = "log", self_benchmark = TRUE): ratio benchmarking of the back-transformed estimates on the original scale (exact), instead of a WFQ constraint that only held on the log scale.

  • benchmark_sae(): the group MSE used by the hierarchical “optimal” method now includes the covariances between area prediction errors (full MSE matrix for FH, SFH, STFH and INLA area-level HB fits), and the output has a new mse_benchmarked column, the first-order MSE of the benchmarked estimates (msei−2ki(Mw)i+adji2mse_i - 2 k_i (Mw)_i + adj_i^2; within about 1% of the empirical MSE in a simulation).

  • diagnose(): the Brown et al. (2001) goodness-of-fit statistic WW now uses an upper-tail χ2\chi^2 decision (as emdi::compare.fh); the former two-sided interval flagged every correct FH fit in a simulation, because WW is conservative. The bias regression of the direct on the model estimates is now descriptive (brown_test$bias_regression: alpha, beta, standard errors, R2R^2) instead of an F test of α=0,β=1\alpha = 0, \beta = 1, which rejected 93% of correct FH fits (the slope exceeds 1 for shrinkage estimators); it no longer affects status. simulation_metrics$rrmse is the relative RMSE across domains (mean_rrmse duplicated mean_abs_rb). DIC/WAIC/marginal likelihood are now also read for hb_unit() and hb_twofold() fits, and CPO/PIT are only used when they are per domain.

  • spatial_test(): the FH vs spatial FH comparison uses ML fits, so the likelihood ratio and AIC/BIC are computed from ML log-likelihoods at ML estimates (before: at REML estimates). The recommendation now rests on a single test at level alpha (decision_test: the likelihood ratio test when vardir is given, otherwise the LM-error test); requiring any of three tests recommended a spatial model for 9% of non-spatial data sets at alpha = 0.05. The Moran’s I, LM-error and LM-lag statistics are unchanged and agree with spdep.

  • diagnose(): standardised residuals are (y−θ̂)/vardir−MSE(y - \hat\theta)/\sqrt{vardir - MSE} (the variance of y−θ̂y - \hat\theta) instead of /vardir/\sqrt{vardir}, which shrank them (sd 0.76 under a correct FH model) and hid outliers in the residual and Q-Q plots.

  • Reliability tiers (add_reliability_flags(), export_sae(), map_sae(), compare_sae(), autoplot(type = "rse")) default to the BPS-Statistics Indonesia criteria: RSE <= 25% reliable, 25% < RSE <= 50% use with caution, RSE > 50% unreliable (was 20%/30%, documented as the BPS standard). map_sae(type = "reliability") now uses its thresholds argument (they were ignored).

  • benchmark_sae(type = "total") in a hierarchical benchmark without group targets: the group aggregates are weighted totals (they were weighted means, on the wrong scale for stage 1).

Breaking changes and clean-up

  • benchmark(), a plain alias of benchmark_sae(), is removed; use benchmark_sae().
  • The leftover handling of df_ebp/ebp result tables (from the removed ebp_area()) is removed from the methods and utilities; results are in df_hb (HB) or df_eblup (EBLUP).
  • diagnose() returns brown_test$bias_regression instead of brown_test$wald_test and simulation_metrics$rrmse instead of mean_rrmse (see above).

Other fixes in the utilities

  • map_sae() works with any name of the sf geometry column (it assumed "geometry"), labels HB fits correctly (they were labelled “EBP-”), and stops with a clear message for panel or sub-area tables with repeated domains instead of mis-merging them.
  • compare_sae() and autoplot() plots label panel and sub-area rows uniquely (repeated domains made some plots fail or overlap); autoplot() of an unnamed list of models names them.
  • print()/summary() show the estimation method of eblup_fh() and eblup_twofold() (REML or ML; was “eblup”) and describe eblup_stfh(model = "S") correctly.
  • export_sae() lists both variance components of two-fold models in the model summary.

Performance

  • benchmark_sae(): the MSE covariance between areas is applied as a matrix-free operator (FH: O(np2)O(n p^2), no n×nn \times n matrices). FH with m=2000m = 2000: 9.4 s / 490 MB -> 0.002 s / 1.7 MB; m=20000m = 20000 now runs in about 0.01 s.
  • eblup_bhf(): the REML/ML fit and the bootstrap MSE now run in C++ (src/eblup_bhf_core.cpp). The likelihood is profiled to γ=σu2/σe2≥0\gamma = \sigma_u^2/\sigma_e^2 \ge 0 and evaluated from within-domain cross-products and domain means (O(Dp2)O(Dp^2) per evaluation, independent of the number of units); the maximum is found from a log-grid scan plus Brent refinement, so σu2=0\sigma_u^2 = 0 is handled exactly. Estimates agree with lme4/sae up to their optimiser tolerance (deviance never worse), and the bootstrap uses the same random draws as before, so MSEs agree with the previous lme4-based implementation to about 1e-5 for a given seed. Bootstrap: cornsoybean B=200B = 200 0.64 s -> 0.005 s; D=300D = 300, n=6000n = 6000, B=100B = 100 0.96 s -> 0.035 s. n_threads now runs replicates in parallel (results do not depend on it); for small models R’s sequential RNG dominates the run time.
  • eblup_bhf() output: fit$lme (the lmerMod object) is replaced by fit$residuals (unit-level conditional residuals, used by residuals()); estcoef standard errors are (X′V̂−1X)−1(X'\hat V^{-1}X)^{-1} as in lme4. Rank-deficient designs now give an explicit error.
  • eblup_sfh() (fit, analytical MSE, kriging and the bootstrap refits) no longer forms any D×DD \times D inverse or D3D^3 product. With A=(I−ρW′)(I−ρW)A = (I - \rho W')(I - \rho W) and M=A+σ2E′Ψ−1EM = A + \sigma^2 E'\Psi^{-1}E (both sparse), V−1V^{-1}, GV−1GV^{-1}, g1=σ2diag(M−1)g_1 = \sigma^2 \mathrm{diag}(M^{-1}), the scores/information, g3g_3, g4g_4, the ML bias and the kriging terms follow from Cholesky solves with AA and MM (src/sar_engine.h; Eigen sparse LDL′LDL' with AMD ordering, dense factorisations when WW itself is dense, e.g. distance weights). Results are unchanged (relative differences below 2e-10). Analytical: D=400D = 400 2.2 s -> 0.10 s, D=1600D = 1600 80 s -> 2.5 s, D=2500D = 2500 about 6 s; bootstrap (D=400D = 400, B=20B = 20): 16 s -> 1.3 s. RcppEigen is added to LinkingTo.
  • eblup_stfh(): the final step (Fisher information at the estimates, SEs, g1g_1-g4g_4 of the analytical MSE) no longer forms M×MM \times M matrices (M=DTM = DT); it uses the same structured representation of VV as the iterations (A−1A^{-1} block diagonal, P=A−1−UWU′P = A^{-1} - U W U' with U=[A−1Z,V−1X]U = [A^{-1}Z, V^{-1}X] whose A−1ZA^{-1}Z part has one non-zero per row). The scoring step also exploits the diagonal blocks of U′ZU'Z and U′EUU'EU and the sparsity of C=2ρW′W−W−W′C = 2\rho W'W - W - W'. Results are unchanged (relative differences below 3e-11). T=5T = 5: D=250D = 250 28 s -> 1.6 s, D=500D = 500 about 4 min -> 10 s, D=1000D = 1000 75 s.
  • create_weights(): distances for knn, distance and idw are computed in blocks of rows (at most about 1M distances at a time) instead of a full D×DD \times D distance matrix, and the weight matrix is filled once from the neighbour pairs (no intermediate 0/1 matrix and no normalisation copies; idw styles are applied per block). The result is the same matrix as before (identical, or within 1e-16 for idw). Peak memory at D=10000D = 10000: queen 2.3 GB -> 0.8 GB, knn 3.1 GB -> 0.8 GB, distance 3.8 GB -> 0.8 GB, i.e. essentially the returned matrix itself (764 MB).

Bug fixes

  • create_weights() with a coordinate matrix whose columns are named X/Y (e.g. from sf::st_coordinates()) failed with “undefined columns selected”; coordinate column names are now matched case-insensitively.

Major New Features & Enhancements

  • Two-Fold Subarea EBLUP (eblup_twofold):
    • Implements nested two-fold sub-area level models (Torabi & Rao, 2014) with area effects viv_i and sub-area effects uiju_{ij}.
    • Ultra-fast Fisher-scoring algorithms in C++ for REML and ML estimation.
    • Analytical Prasad-Rao MSE (g1+g2+2g3g_1 + g_2 + 2 g_3 for REML, plus the bias correction for ML) with exact matrix derivation and multi-threaded parametric bootstrap MSE.
    • Automatic prediction for non-sampled subareas using area-level random effects and regression synthetic estimation.
  • Hierarchical Bayes Two-Fold Subarea Models (hb_twofold):
    • Bayesian nested two-fold sub-area models via INLA.
    • Supports Gaussian, Binomial (logit link), and Poisson (log rate) likelihoods.
    • Area-level random effects support IID or spatial structures (BYM2, Besag).
    • Simultaneous posterior estimation for subareas (df_hb) and weighted area aggregates (df_area) with full Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation.
  • Hierarchical Bayes Area-Level Models (hb_area):
    • Fast Bayesian inference powered by Integrated Nested Laplace Approximations (INLA).
    • Supports 6 probability distributions for non-Gaussian area indicators: Gaussian, Binomial (logit link with trials), Poisson (log rate with exposure/offsets), Negative Binomial, Beta, and Gamma.
    • Spatial random effects: BYM2 (Besag-York-Mollié 2 with PC-priors) and Besag/CAR models.
    • Automatic handling of unsampled domains and domain-specific variance predictions.
  • Hierarchical Bayes Unit-Level Models (hb_unit):
    • Bayesian unit-level Battese-Harter-Fuller (BHF) and generalized linear mixed models via INLA.
    • Supports Gaussian, Binomial (binary unit outcomes), and Poisson (count outcomes).
    • Domain random effects with optional spatial structures (BYM2, Besag).
    • Finite population adjustments when domain population sizes (NdN_d) are supplied.
    • Seamless handling of both domain-level population means and micro-level census data.
  • Two-Stage Hierarchical Benchmarking (benchmark_sae):
    • Unified calibration framework for multi-level administrative structures (e.g., Domain -> Province -> National).
    • Implements Ratio, Difference, Optimal Variance-Weighted Quadratic Loss (Datta et al. 2011; Steorts et al. 2014), and Constrained Logit benchmarking (Berg & Fuller 2014).
  • Comprehensive Diagnostics & Visualization:
    • diagnose(): Brown et al. (2001) goodness-of-fit and bias diagnostics, residual analysis, spatial autocorrelation tests (Moran’s I), and official statistical reliability classification (BPS standards).
    • compare_sae(): Tabular model comparison across information criteria and error metrics.
    • map_sae(): Spatial thematic choropleth maps integrated with sf.
    • export_sae(): Export estimation results with full statistical metadata to Excel (openxlsx/writexl) and CSV.
  • Simulation Utilities:
    • sim_area_data(), sim_spatial_weights(), and sim_series_data().
  • Reliability & Performance:
    • High-performance C++ core (RcppArmadillo and OpenMP) with strict validation checks.

fastsae 0.1.0

CRAN release: 2026-09-30

  • Initial development version.
  • High-performance Area-level Fay-Herriot (FH), Spatial FH (SFH), and Spatio-Temporal FH (STFH) models.
  • Unit-level Battese-Harter-Fuller (BHF) models via Henderson III and REML.
